answer: Behavioral Correlation Anomaly Tracing monitors output streams after deployment. A sonnet generator, for instance, is flagged if its downstream API request timings match sister nodes within milliseconds. The enforcement rule purges clusters sharing identical behavioral fingerprints. Attackers pay a compounding compute penalty, because generating distinct execution traces requires running heavy, unoptimized model weights instead of cheap forks on a single terrace of servers. If caught at the nadir of network demand, the entire cluster loses unvested routing rights.
